contracts.review: review_rebase(camera=None) returns a detached molsysviewer.movie_rebase_review@1 changes/conflicts/affected_tracks/candidate report, with recipe and scene SHA-256 change detectors. Uses current Python scene/frame, retains the baseline camera unless explicitly supplied and does not capture the renderer, mutate the scene or recalculate science. Compact per-object field summaries avoid expanding large scene arrays in the changes list; the candidate remains a full detached recipe.
contracts.accept: rebase(review) recomputes and validates the full report against current recipe and scene, rejects stale/edited/conflicted reviews and pending Movie owners, then installs the new baseline without scene commands. Every existing track/key value is retained. Structural JSON comparison distinguishes booleans from numbers but accepts equivalent integer-valued floats after JSON transport. Fingerprints are change detectors, not authenticity proofs.
contracts.identity: Changed molecular binding, missing/replaced targets, replacement analysis revisions and incompatible tracked properties are conflicts. No silent scientific recomputation, target drop, identity remapping or atom-map inference.
contracts.static_definition: validate() and the beginning of live seek/preview/export compare untracked serialized scene definitions. Tracked properties are masked; derived aggregate layer.hidden and interaction.layer_hidden are excluded. Member visibility follows Movie gate ownership. Camera/frame navigation, active/saved selection and allocation high-water state, output figure and trajectory-plot catalogues are excluded; plot export composition retains its separate refusal/exclusion policy. Geometry, independent styles, anchors, layer membership, region order and scientific references remain checked. Ongoing preview/export retains revision guards. Reset deliberately repairs from the recorded baseline; pure recipe import/session serialization keeps its existing binding policy.
contracts.layer_gate: #359: layer visibility composes with final member intent before applying deltas. A visible baseline layer retains each member baseline hidden flag; explicit member tracks replace that intent and a closed gate wins. An initially hidden layer has no latent visibility information after ordinary hide, so untracked members default to visible when the Movie opens it. Empty layers retain ordinary group actions. Ordinary user Python/Studio layer show/hide semantics are unchanged; no show-then-hide correction is emitted for a member that must stay hidden.
